top_choice_rationale: Anne Carson (P001) is the only writer on the slate. On the common criteria her case rests on the writing, not on the shared opening ranking. Her voice is recognisable in a few lines. In Autobiography of Red, as I understand it from public knowledge, the verse-novel form carries the Geryon material as a modern love story. In Nox, translation, commentary and archival fragments are the means by which the elegy mourns. Loss, desire, inheritance and the limits of translation recur across verse, essay, drama and versions from Greek, which I read as one sustained project. The main reservation is maturity: I cannot establish whether her later books deepen the project or refine a settled method. I have not independently verified those texts, and I keep that as an open uncertainty rather than assuming it away. Other risks are the dependence on typography and allusion in translation, and where to draw the line between original writing, translation and scholarship. The citation should credit her own original lyric, verse narrative and essay, including Nox with translation as method, and should name the seriousness about grief and desire so that it does not read as a prize for erudition. On balance, this oeuvre is distinctive and substantial enough that awarding it is preferable to no award. P000 is ranked second, and only because the maturity question is unresolved.
